title: Google will switch off Search for schools that reject its AI tools
tldr: Google will turn its AI tools off by default for K-12 student accounts, but schools that keep them off also lose Google Search, because Google treats Search and AI as one product.
byline: TechCrunch, The Verge, Ars Technica

title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
tldr: An open-weight Qwen model, driven through a carefully designed tool harness and with no privileged inputs, beats the published GPT-6 Astra result on the RoboDojo robot benchmark.
byline: Jiarui Yuan, Yuxin Zuo, Xiaoyu Huang et al. · Tsinghua University, UC Berkeley

title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
tldr: A 240-task benchmark scores AI agents as teammates and finds that even the best model reaches only 82.2 out of 100, with strong models caving under social pressure and keeping inherited cheating.
byline: Sean Wu, Aneesh Pappu, Jiaru Zou et al. · Stanford University, University of Oxford, MIT

title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
tldr: Muon beats AdamW at pretraining loss but, with enough pretraining data, AdamW models fine-tune better, and the crossover arrives sooner as models grow.
byline: Catherine Li, Jingchu Gai, Andrej Risteski et al.

title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
tldr: DR Pixel does deep research directly on rendered page images instead of OCR text, and a step-weighted fine-tuning method lifts a 27B open model to GPT-5.4-level accuracy.
byline: Tiansheng Hu, Yichuan Wang, James V. Talwar et al. · NYU Shanghai, UC Berkeley, Rational Dynamics

title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Turning a judge's per-turn text feedback into a self-distillation signal, only on failing turns and alongside normal RL rewards, teaches coding agents behaviors that plain RL never discovers.
byline: Kevin Frans, Alexander M Rush, Sergey Levine et al. · Cursor Research, UC Berkeley

title: Anthropic's amended IPO filing says it may imminently reach its own "dramatically accelerated progress" threshold
tldr: In a revised S-1/A filed Monday, Anthropic wrote that its internal estimates suggest it may imminently meet the Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of AI-driven dramatically accelerated progress, while saying no current model crosses it.
byline: TechCrunch

title: Researchers show GPT-6 Astra can read and directly edit neural network weights, lifting a small Qwen model's math score
tldr: A blog post reports that GPT-6 Astra, without writing training loops, identified a flaw in Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and fixed it by editing 0.016% of them, raising MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%.
byline: Weight-Space Programming blog post

title: Hinted Scaling Laws
tldr: Giving models partial reference solutions turns a hard benchmark into a smooth family of easier ones, letting scaling laws fit on small, near-zero-accuracy models forecast large-model benchmark accuracy with far lower error.
byline: Suze van Adrichem, Luke Bailey, Rohith Kuditipudi et al. · Stanford University

title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
tldr: Wave Forcing lets several video chunks denoise at once on different GPUs, with earlier chunks serving as cleaner context for later ones, reaching about 135 end-to-end frames per second on eight H200 GPUs.
byline: Yijie Jin, Yuxuan Liu, Jiajun Xu et al. · Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Peking University

title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
tldr: In a video-plus-action world model, videos of new tasks without action labels lift out-of-distribution success on RoboTwin 2.0 from 25% to 56%, and one labeled demonstration per task lifts it to 71%.
byline: Jun Cen, Yubo Guo, Hao Li et al. · Joy Future Academy

title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
tldr: Jet-QSparse stores the KV cache in 4-bit NVFP4 and aggregates values from selected blocks only, giving 1.94 times faster decoding and 2.58 to 2.76 times cache capacity without training.
byline: Haozhan Tang, Hao Kang, Meng Lu et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, Virginia Tech, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
tldr: CoworkOS is an open agent harness that separates strategy from execution management, matches or beats Codex-style harnesses on 12 benchmarks, and drives five rounds of automated post-training that lifted a Qwen model by 9.76 points.
byline: Jiajie Jin, Guanting Dong, Chengjun Pan et al. · Renmin University of China, Fudan University, Peking University

title: Marvell agrees to buy optical-chip maker Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal
tldr: Marvell will acquire laser and optical-module maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion, a bet that AI data centers are moving from copper to integrated optical connectivity.
byline: Marvell Investor Relations

title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
tldr: LARC lets a unified image model think in continuous hidden states instead of text before drawing, trained with a curriculum and a self-supervised information-gain reward, and it improves with more thinking.
byline: Byungwoo Jeon, Yoonwoo Jeong, Hyunseok Lee et al. · KAIST, POSTECH, RLWRLD

title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
tldr: ID-WM plans long tasks by using diffusion noise as an abstract action that picks reachable subgoals, while a second model converts each hop into precise actions.
byline: Gaoyue Zhou, Yvonne Wu, Zichen Jeff Cui et al. · New York University (Courant Institute), Meta FAIR, AMI Labs

title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
tldr: CaPtain turns a 4B open vision-language model, which initially solves nothing, into a robot agent that writes code against low-level primitives, using synthetic supervision and reinforcement learning with a simulator-informed critic.
byline: Yijia Fan, Xilin He, Yilei Jiang et al. · Chinese University of Hong Kong (MMLab), NovaXBot

title: Chronos-2: A foundation model for multivariate time series forecasting
tldr: Chronos-2 is a 120M-parameter zero-shot forecaster that uses group attention to learn relationships among related series and covariates in context, trained only on synthetic multivariate data.
byline: Abdul Fatir Ansari, Oleksandr Shchur, Jaris Küken et al. · Amazon Web Services, University of Freiburg, Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry

title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
tldr: ACCT converts a small model's already-computed context cache into a compressed cache that a larger model in the same family can use directly, skipping the large model's expensive prefill.
byline: Yuzhe Liu, Haolin Tian, Tonghan Wang · Tsinghua University

title: OpenAI reportedly cuts its new funding round's target to $20 billion as investors cool
tldr: The Financial Times reports OpenAI lowered its new round's target from $30 billion to $20 billion, and the Wall Street Journal says $11 billion is secured, during a tech-stock selloff over AI spending.
byline: TechCrunch, The Next Web

title: Google's Project Suncatcher satellite answers its first prompt, running Gemma 4 on a TPU in orbit
tldr: Google's first Project Suncatcher prototype, carrying four TPUs, answered a prompt from orbit with Gemma 4, starting tests of whether data-center AI chips can survive heat and radiation in space.
byline: TechCrunch, The Verge

title: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models for Agentic AI
tldr: NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3.5 Super, a 120B-parameter hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts with 12B active, adds a built-in drafter and 4-bit weights, reaching 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro.
byline: NVIDIA, Aastha Jhunjhunwala, Aayushi Ashokkumar Srivastava et al. · NVIDIA

title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
tldr: Weight normalization's pretraining gains over weight decay come mostly from its effective learning-rate trajectory; scheduling that quantity with a theory-derived inverse-square-root shape (AIR) cuts MoE loss about 0.01 below cosine.
byline: Qifan Yu, Xinyu Ma, Xingyan Bin et al. · ByteDance Seed, Peking University

title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
tldr: Exponential residual flows give discrete diffusion language models an analogue of the probability-flow ODE: after one random draw, sampling is deterministic yet provably keeps the right distributions, enabling consistency distillation.
byline: Samson Gourevitch, Yazid Janati, Eric Moulines et al. · École polytechnique, MBZUAI, EPITA

title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
tldr: Training a chatbot to write an explicit, rule-checkable safety decision before it replies turns the shallowness of safety alignment into a defense against multi-turn jailbreaks, without a judge model in the reward.
byline: Qiyao Ma, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang et al. · Microsoft Research, University of California, Davis

title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
tldr: In compute-matched experiments, spending part of a pretraining budget on synthetic pre-pretraining never beats spending it on natural text, and an earlier reported gain disappears once the baseline's initialization is improved.
byline: Alexander Stern, Tim Rocktäschel, Acyr Locatelli et al. · Cohere, UCL AI Centre, MIT
